Definition: from G5271; acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy"):--condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy.
BiblicalUsage: hypókrisis is the word for hypocrisy, play-acting, deceit. In Matthew 23:28, the text says "but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity." In Mark 12:15, the text says "knowing their hypocrisy."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: hypókrisis tells me that truth is not whatever we feel; it is what God has said, and it stands. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Render to Caesar; Paul Confronts Peter at Antioch
